correctness.rationale: For all independent Bernoulli variables with success probabilities \(p,q\in[0,1]\), the three-atom PMF gives exact total-variation distances \(pq\) to \(\operatorname{Bin}(1,p+q-pq)\) and \((\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\) to \(\operatorname{Bin}(2,\sqrt{pq})\). If \(pq<1/4\) the former is strict; if \(pq\ge1/4\), order \(p\ge q\) to obtain \(q\ge1/(4p)\ge1/4\) and \(\sqrt p-\sqrt q\le1/2\), with equality only at \((p,q)=(1,1/4)\). At that pair, a one-trial binomial misses the \(1/4\) mass at two; every binomial with integer trial count \(m\ge2\) has singleton mass \(P\{1\}\le((m-1)/m)^{m-1}\le1/2\), while the source mass at one is \(3/4\). These facts prove the universal lower bound and exact extremizers. The maximal singleton inequality follows by calculus and the binomial theorem. The standalone exact-Fraction verifier replayed 655 low-branch, 174 high-branch, and 3250 extremal cases; these finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The complete inspected Jaramillo–Melbourne, Roos, and Choi–Xia texts treat bounds or constructions under fixed trial counts, mean matching, or an open unrestricted parameter-selection question. They do not state, and their cited bounds do not logically deliver, the universal sharp radius \(1/4\) for all two-coin sums against the union of binomials of all trial counts, nor uniqueness of the deterministic-quarter extremizers. Searches of indexed primary literature and published mathematical findings found no directly covering statement; this is limited same-model originality screening rather than a proof of global priority. Ehm (1991) and other older literature remain residual risks.
residual_risks: The 1991 Ehm article is strongly thematically relevant but complete text was inaccessible. Its abstract limits the stated program to same-count mean-matched approximation; an unadvertised stronger or equivalent special-case statement cannot be excluded.

An equivalent exact radius or extremal two-coin calculation may exist in older or unindexed probability-approximation literature, under a different name, or in unpublished work. Database partitioning/search absence does not establish priority.

value.rationale: The natural directed total-variation covering radius from the two-trial heterogeneous Bernoulli-sum family to all binomial laws is a motivated extremal approximation invariant: primary literature explicitly poses optimal binomial parameter choice, while classical bounds do not determine this unrestricted radius. The theorem supplies a nonasymptotic best-possible uniform \(1/4\) guarantee, proves that one or two trial binomials suffice for that guarantee, identifies the unique worst input laws up to parameter interchange, and establishes why any larger binomial trial count cannot avoid the obstruction at those inputs. The boundary probability \(1/4\) follows from the competing zero-mass and two-mass matchings against a maximal singleton-mass constraint, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. Pointwise optimization and larger source support remain outside scope.
